title: Tree Canopy and Crime in LA
gallery_text: Using Los Angeles census blocks, tree canopy data, and crime records from January to July 2024, this map explores the spatial relationship between urban tree coverage and crime patterns across the City of Los Angeles.
description: This map was created using data collected from GeoHub LA City and Los Angeles Open Data, including Crime Data from 2020 to 2024, Percent Tree Canopy, and LA City 2020 Census Blocks. For the crime data, I specifically filtered the records to a shorter time period, from January 2024 to July 2024, to focus on more recent crime patterns. The map is intended to explore the relationship between crime and tree canopy coverage at the census block level across the City of Los Angeles. By juxtaposing proportional symbols representing crime counts with a choropleth map of tree canopy coverage, the map reveals a potential spatial pattern: areas with higher tree canopy coverage often have lower concentrations of crime, while areas with lower tree canopy coverage tend to have higher crime counts.
